hints.title: Decomposition Slicing Overhead Obstacle
hints.text: Decomposing into primitive blocks by substring slicing requires multiple allocations. How can tracking the nesting depth with a counter determine whether each bracket belongs to the outer shell in a single pass?

hints.title: Depth Boundary Invariant
hints.text: An opening bracket '(' is outermost if and only if depth is 0 before it is added. A closing bracket ')' is outermost if and only if depth becomes 0 after it is closed.

hints.title: Depth Filter Procedure
hints.text: Initialize depth to 0 and an output string list. For each character, if '(', append to output only if depth > 0, then increment depth. If ')', decrement depth, and append to output only if depth > 0. Return the joined output.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass accumulating non-outermost characters into the result.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Partitioning the string by substring slicing and copying creates multiple intermediate strings, increasing memory overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct conditional character emission in a single linear pass uses optimal O(N) time and memory for output.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that outermost parentheses correspond precisely to transitions to/from depth 0.
